quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that all traffic must flow in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. You must obey these signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on the interstate?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Keep driving and take the next exit instead.

questions.question: How often must vehicles be inspected?

options.text: Once every four years
Once every three years
Once every two years
Once every year

questions.correctAnswerText: Once every year
questions.explanation: Vehicles must be inspected once a year during your birth month. Schedule an appointment at an official inspection station.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow a fire truck with its siren on closer than ____ feet.

options.text: One mile
1,000 feet
750 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: You must stay at least 500 feet away from a fire truck responding to an emergency. Do not park your vehicle within one block of where a fire truck has stopped.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your right wheels leave the pavement. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently guide the vehicle back onto the road using a small steering wheel turn. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Obey the flagger's directions in construction zones. Ignoring them is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians cross first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging ahead.
Multiple turns ahead.
Lane is shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge from the right. Be prepared to safely let traffic merge in front of you.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink by saying, "I'm driving."
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices once you have started drinking.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than normal traffic.
Making sudden, quick stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than normal traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What helps drivers avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave highways as soon as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Reduce speed and increase distance between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed and increase distance between cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Reducing speed and increasing distance between your vehicle and others are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad winter conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign blocking it.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without blocking other traffic.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what happens?

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver may then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or sounds of a train.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles go first when they use a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass if no oncoming cars are coming.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross without an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful around children. They may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: If a car is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get attention. If the other car does not move, steer right to escape. Steering left could cause a crash if the other driver also corrects. Brake hard to reduce speed and impact.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and go carefully.
Wait until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another way across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross if a train is near or going fast. This applies even if there are no signals or they are not working.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very rare.
Very dangerous.
Not a real concern.
As safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to driving prevents crashes.

questions.question: Lanes going the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting danger and acting to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to protect yourself.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to get around traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting danger and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and act before a crash happens. It helps you handle aggressive, careless, or unsafe drivers.

questions.question: On a two-lane road with no bike lanes, how do you safely pass a bicyclist?

options.text: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
Drive straight. It is the bicyclist's job to move.
Wait until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like any other vehicle with enough space. Leave at least 3 feet on regular roads or 5 feet on higher-speed roads or with groups. Do not honk as it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers to be careful when roads are wet and slippery.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop.
Use crosswalks only when they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of people.
Certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes should merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of people.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. HOV lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Braking too much.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires become less able to clear water from the road. If you drive too fast, your tires may lose grip and slide on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.
The vehicle traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals or signs, you must yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.
